| [LIT-115](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-115.md) v5 | Duality as a category-theoretic concept | Corfield (2015), DOI-10.1016/j.shpsb.2015.07.004. A short programmatic paper. Its thesis is that category theory, not set theory, is the framework in which the scattered instances of mathematical duality can be drawn together. The constructions in §3 (dual adjunctions restricting to dual equivalences on fixed points, truth-value-enriched Galois connections, Isbell conjugation, dualising objects "keeping summer and winter homes") all "revolve around" adjunction, though Corfield expects no "single monolithic account" (p. 59–60). On his usage, 'duality' is reserved for "involution with some form of structural reversal" (p. 57), so several physicists' dualities (homological mirror symmetry as an A∞-equivalence, mirror symmetry's Z2 on the Hodge diamond, S-duality as a vestige of SL(2,Z)) are better called equivalences or symmetries. | [LIT-151](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-151.md) v2 | Stating Structural Realism: Mathematics-First Approaches to Physics and Metaphysics | Wallace (2021), DOI-10.1111/phpe.12172. Wallace argues that reading a physical theory "math-first", as mathematical models plus representation rather than as sentences aiming at truth, already makes scientific realism structural. Math-first theoretical equivalence and reduction (as instantiation) are coarse-grained enough to dissolve the standard underdetermination and theory-change objections. On this footing epistemic and ontic structural realism differ only in whether metaphysics itself is language-first or math-first. On math-first OSR, objects are whatever the best "predicate precisification" of a theory quantifies over, real patterns are defined through instantiation plus best precisification, and ontology is scale-relative. At every non-fundamental level the two versions coincide. The paper is explicitly a statement of the position, not a defence of it. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-142](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-142.md)); worth reading as the sharpest statement of what structural realism could mean once theories are taken math-first. It gives precise definitions of math-first ESR/OSR and of real patterns, its diagnosis of why priority-thesis OSR drifted is useful, and it is candid about the undeveloped notion of mathematical equivalence it relies on. |
| [LIT-154](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-154.md) v3 | Criteria of Identity and Structuralist Ontology | Leitgeb & Ladyman (2007), DOI-10.1093/philmat/nkm039. Graph theory counts unlabelled graphs whose nodes, or whose isomorphic connected components, cannot be told apart even by an irreflexive relation. Examples are the edgeless two-node graph G′ and any graph with two or more isolated nodes (11 of the 156 unlabelled 6-node graphs). Mathematicians treat these as determinately distinct objects, so the authors conclude that the identity or difference of places in a structure is given by the structure itself, with identity counted among its relations, and not by any criterion of identity. The argument appeals to mathematical practice; it is not a proof. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-133](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-133.md)); worth reading as the short, standard counterexample to weak-discernibility versions of the PII for mathematical structuralism. | [LIT-222](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-222.md) v2 | No categorial support for radical ontic structural realism | Lam & Wüthrich (2015), DOI-10.1093/bjps/axt053. Lam and Wüthrich argue that category theory gives radical OSR no support. Identifying objects with identity arrows is relabelling (§3). Generalized elements X → A exist in every category, so elements are not eliminated (§4). Categories without products also lose set-style relations, "throwing out the relations with the relata" (§4). Morphisms relate C-objects, not the elements that stand for physical relata, and they "only distinguish isomorphism classes of structures" (§5). Bain's GR and TQFT cases eliminate at most spacetime points, not relata tout court (§§6–7). They conclude that category theory "offers little if any comfort to ROSR" (abstract) and favour "balanced" OSR. The Yoneda lemma is not named, although §§4–5 state two of its consequences. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-194](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-194.md)); Worth reading as the most careful direct refutation of Bain (yo2). | [LIT-223](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-223.md) v2 | Category-theoretic structure and radical ontic structural realism | Bain (2013), DOI-10.1007/s11229-011-9896-6. | [LIT-3221](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3221.md) | Realizability: a historical essay | Van Oosten (2002) sketches the history of realizability from Kleene's 1945 paper to the effective topos. He states Kleene's definition clause by clause: a realizer of an existential is a pair of a witness and a realizer of its instance, a realizer of an implication or universal a program, a realizer of a true atomic sentence the number 0. Realizability was "designed to handle 'information' about formulas rather than proofs", and Kleene set aside Heyting's proof interpretation to build it. Kreisel's modified realizability (1959) types the realizers by the formula's form, and in Hyland's effective topos Kleene's realizability is the truth definition for arithmetic. Read as the stand-in for Kleene 1945 ([LIT-3213](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3213.md)) for [LEAD-215](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-215.md); it bears on [CLAIM-949](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-949.md) and on the terms witness and certificate ([TERM-154](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-154.md), [TERM-153](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-153.md)). | Active — read in full 2026-11-22 ([NOTE-2420](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2420.md)) from the author's copy on his Utrecht page; worth reading as the shortest reliable statement of Kleene's 1945 realizability, clause by clause, and of what became of it: formalized and glued realizability, Kreisel's typed (modified) realizability ten years before "formulae as types", and the effective topos, in which Kleene's realizability is the truth definition of arithmetic. | [LIT-3229](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3229.md) v2 | Zur Deutung der intuitionistischen Logik | Kolmogorov (as Kolmogoroff, 1932), Mathematische Zeitschrift 35, read in [NOTE-2422](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2422.md). Beside the logic of theoretical statements there is a calculus of problems (Aufgabenrechnung), whose formulas are problems and whose rules systematize schemes of solution; it needs no intuitionist assumptions and "nach der Form" coincides with Heyting's intuitionistic logic. In §2 he argues that the objects of intuitionistic logic are really problems, not statements. Problems, unlike proved statements, have no notion of correctness. The reading tests [CLAIM-949](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-949.md)'s correspondence of a question with a problem ([THEORY-2308](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2308.md), [ARG-245](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-245.md)). | Active — read in full 2026-11-22 ([NOTE-2422](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2422.md)) from the scan the Göttingen State and University Library's digitization centre (GDZ) serves for research use; worth reading as the source of the reading of intuitionistic logic as a calculus of problems, and for the distinction it keeps, and says Heyting lacked, between statements and problems. |
| [LIT-3232](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3232.md) | Intuitionistic Type Theory | Martin-Löf, P. (1984), Intuitionistic Type Theory, notes by Giovanni Sambin of lectures given in Padua in June 1980, Bibliopolis, Naples (Studies in Proof Theory). Four forms of judgement, A set, A = B, a ∈ A and a = b ∈ A, each read four ways: a set and its element, a proposition and its proof, an intention and its fulfilment, a problem and its solution, with "a is a program ... which meets the specification A" (p. 6). A set is defined by how its canonical elements are formed; an element is a method that yields one; propositions and sets are identified. A proof of an existential is a pair of a witness and a proof that it satisfies the property, and the set of a ∈ A such that B(a) has such pairs as its elements, "the witnessing information" (p. 53). Universes are sets of codes of sets, closed under the set-forming operations; there is no set of all sets, and U is not an element of U. Read in [NOTE-2419](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2419.md) for [LEAD-215](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-215.md)'s test of [CLAIM-949](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-949.md); the reading is [THEORY-2307](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2307.md). | Active — read 2026-11-25 (Skimmed: the introduction, the explanations of the forms of judgement, propositions as sets, the cartesian product and disjoint union with their applications, the notion of such that and universes closely, pp. i–54, 64, 69–70 and 87–91; the rest at the level of rules and examples) from a scan hosted by a Carnegie Mellon course, OCR'd; worth reading as the source of the judgement forms and the propositions-as-sets reading on which [LEAD-215](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-215.md)'s test of [CLAIM-949](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-949.md) turns, and as the place where a set read as a specification and its elements as programs that meet it is said in so many words. |
